clue.text: Wretched housing left at the back of resort

indicators.note: at the back of places the letter for left after the resort's name

parts.note: Hove is a seaside resort beside Brighton on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Run-down lodgings are tucked away behind a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside town in Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, miserable dwelling, so it is poor housing.

clue.text: Unwelcome information about oneself, in fact

parts.note: to be home means to be in, not out
a truth is a fact

explanation.surface: Being told an unwelcome fact about yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A home truth is an unpleasant fact about one's own faults that someone else points out.

clue.text: Some have no motive for spite

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people act out of malice with no reason at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'for spite' takes in 'for', a link word; the definition that substitutes for the answer is just 'spite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is bitter malice, a synonym of spite.

clue.text: Cooking plum tarts, this will signal that time is up

definitions.text: this will signal that time is up

indicators.note: Cooking suggests the fruit and pastry words are being worked into something new

explanation.surface: When the plum tarts are baking, a timer goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Trump is the trumpet call said to announce the Day of Judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet blast at the end of the world announces that mortal life is over.

clue.text: Accommodation arranged by Ld. Balfour

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the two words that follow are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters L and D

explanation.surface: Lord Balfour has booked somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ld.' looks like a title for the statesman Balfour, but its two letters join BALFOUR as the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Full board is a kind of hotel lodging where every meal is included.

clue.text: Moth perhaps circling wide over a mown area

indicators.note: circling means the fairy's name goes around the other letters

parts.note: Moth is one of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, puts the letter for wide above the letter A

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wide

explanation.surface: An insect flutters round over a cut lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moth' is not an insect but a fairy from A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairway is the closely cut stretch of a golf course between tee and green.

clue.text: The end of one flight, or break between two

explanation.surface: A flight ends, or there is a pause between two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's touchdown ends its journey; a platform between two flights of stairs breaks the climb.

clue.text: Green material obtained from trees, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it sounds

parts.note: bays are laurel trees

explanation.surface: A green fabric is said to be made from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Baize is the green woollen cloth used to cover snooker and card tables.

clue.text: During the spring the sea will be in poor condition

definitions.text: During the spring the sea will be

explanation.surface: Tides in spring leave the sea in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: At spring tides the sea falls further than usual at low tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring tides bring the lowest falls of water; the phrase also means in a weak or depressed state.

clue.text: The old fellow about to be the oldest member

indicators.note: about means the fellow's word goes around the old article

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
ye is an old form of the word the

explanation.surface: An elderly man is about to become the senior member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' is not an old person: it means an old spelling of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior or respected member of a group.

clue.text: — carelessly misusing name

indicators.note: carelessly suggests the letters are thrown together in a jumbled new order

explanation.surface: Someone sloppily gets a name wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash at the start of the clue is itself the definition: the printed symbol is what the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: The short horizontal stroke printed is the symbol used for subtraction in arithmetic.

clue.text: The country's leaders featured in intrigue throughout all last year

indicators.note: leaders points to the first letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A nation's rulers have been scheming for the whole of the past year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' seems to mean politicians, but it asks for the opening letters of the next five words.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a European nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Try to persuade office worker to start on the typewriter

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: start on asks for the opening letter of the word typewriter

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes a stand-in secretary into beginning some typing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or coax them into doing something.

clue.text: Reduce the value of record

explanation.surface: An accountant cuts an asset's book value and notes it.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting, to write down an asset is to lower its stated worth; to put something on paper is to note it.

clue.text: Leader you both backed, sacrificing love for a country

indicators.note: love is O, as in a tennis score of nil, and it is given up for the letter A
both backed says each of the two words before it is turned round where it stands

parts.note: a guru is a spiritual leader or teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chief and his follower both reverse, giving up romance for a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both backed' reverses each piece in place, giving URUG and UOY; 'sacrificing love for a' then swaps the O (love, nil in tennis) for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Uruguay is a South American nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: University record broken by rising musical — leading man's a humble clerk

indicators.note: broken by means the university and record letters are split open by the others

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the musical's name is read upwards

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
the leading man of a show is a he, a male

explanation.surface: A college record is interrupted by a show on the up, whose star is a meek office worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' signals a reversal and 'broken by' an insertion. Uriah Heep is the fawning, falsely humble clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep, the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, constantly claims to be very humble.

clue.text: Cove with weapon concealed in clothing

indicators.note: concealed says the weapon is hidden inside the word for the man

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or fellow, like gent
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A chap is hiding a gun in his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cove' here is not a bay but old British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any article of clothing, such as a coat or dress.

clue.text: Coming back over the course

parts.note: re means about or concerning, much as over does in 'argue over'
a current is the course or flow of water or air

explanation.surface: A runner returns to the track for another lap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurrent happens again and again, returning repeatedly.

clue.text: Something like a magnolia growing from centre of bulb in Essex town

indicators.note: in says the central letters go inside the name of the town

parts.note: Tiptree is a town in the English county of Essex, known for its jam

indicators.note: centre of picks out the two middle letters of the word bulb

explanation.surface: A flowering plant springs from the heart of a bulb in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: TIPTREE is a small town in Essex, a county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip tree belongs to the magnolia family and has similar large cup-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Grip the bend

explanation.surface: Someone holds tight on a sharp corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a clip that holds hair in place; a hairpin bend is a very sharp turn in a road.

clue.text: Irritated, was first to support demand

indicators.note: to support means sitting beneath, in a down clue placed below the other word

parts.note: a need is a requirement or demand
to have led is to have been in front, first

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed after going first to back a request.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to support' puts LED underneath NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means annoyed or provoked, as if pricked repeatedly.

clue.text: In a month one noise-maker cut the sound level

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is chopped off the word for the noise-maker

parts.note: a bell is something that makes a noise

explanation.surface: During a particular month a loud device was trimmed to bring down the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' shortens BELL to BEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the unit used to measure loudness, a measure of how loud something is.

clue.text: File is held up by one administering treatment

indicators.note: held says the turned word sits inside the word for the person giving treatment

parts.note: a doser is one who gives doses of medicine

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word is is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical record is being kept back by someone giving treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held ... by' is split around 'up': the container's two words sit either side of the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of papers on a person or subject.

clue.text: I state composer's son is still working

parts.note: NH is the postal abbreviation for New Hampshire, a US state
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a musician's child has not yet retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I state' looks like 'I declare', but 'state' gives NH, New Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in harness is to be at work, like a horse still hitched up.

clue.text: Fish, almost entirely perfect

parts.note: an ide is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is left off

parts.note: all means entirely, as in 'all alone'

explanation.surface: A fish is very nearly flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, the best possible.

clue.text: Free climbing say in mountain range

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Unroped climbing in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow chain of hills or the crest of a mountain line.

clue.text: Go over and back a horse

indicators.note: back says the word for the horse is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pacer is a horse trained to a pacing gait in harness racing

explanation.surface: Someone studies the form again before betting on a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back a horse' looks like placing a bet, but 'back' reverses the word for the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, going through the main points once more.

clue.text: Chinese weight like an ounce

explanation.surface: An Asian measure compared with an imperial one.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce here is the snow leopard, not the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A catty is a Chinese unit of weight; the ounce, or snow leopard, is a big feline, so like a cat.

clue.text: Editor admits people may be correct

indicators.note: admits means the abbreviation takes the people inside it

parts.note: men is used for people, as in 'all men are equal'

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor concedes the public could be right.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or improve it.

clue.text: The queen's favourite isle — Crete, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters turn up in an unexpected new arrangement

explanation.surface: The monarch's best-loved island is, unexpectedly, Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earl of Leicester, Robert Dudley, was famously the favourite of Queen Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was the courtier most favoured by Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Pearl-diver not very upset — he sees what you say

indicators.note: upset says the remaining letters are knocked over into a new order
not says the letter for very is dropped from the diver's name

explanation.surface: A diver who is only mildly troubled watches people's words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' removes V from PEARLDIVER; 'upset' rearranges the remaining PEARLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can read lips follows speech by watching mouth movements.

clue.text: "Season" they say, "You can season with this"

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a season is a time of year

explanation.surface: People pun on 'season', saying it is something you put in food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' first means a period of time, then cooking with herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb is used to flavour food, so cooks add it to dishes.
